A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same xRFM research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including identification of internal reporting inconsistencies in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original TALENT and meta-test evaluations, runtime measurements, synthetic experiments and AGOP interpretability case studies.

after.justification: v2 reports updated TALENT and meta-test outcomes, additional TabArena-Lite evaluations, and retained synthetic and interpretability results.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces separate L1/product and L2/isotropic adaptive-bandwidth rules with scaling using the selected Lp norm. Table A.1 also permits intermediate kernel norm orders. These are limited leaf-model refinements; AGOP learning, balanced tree partitioning and inference remain structurally unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on the 51-dataset TabArena-Lite collection, comprising 13 regression and 38 classification datasets, alongside the retained TALENT and large meta-test benchmarks. This substantially expands reported benchmark coverage, although overlap between collections is not enumerated and 51 should not be interpreted as a net count of new datasets.

E2.justification: The added TabArena comparisons evaluate previously unevaluated comparators including AutoGluon 1.3, TabDPT, TabM, ExtraTrees and EBM (Tables B.8–B.9). Existing TALENT and meta-test comparator memberships remain; MLP and ResNet are merely relabeled MLP-RTDL and ResNet-RTDL in the meta-test tables.

E3.justification: TabArena-Lite introduces AUROC, multiclass log-loss, Elo aggregation, median inference-time comparisons and default/tuned/T+E configurations. Table A.1 also revises existing benchmarks' kernel search distributions and changes early-stop multipliers from 1.06/1.05 to 1.1. These are reported setting changes, without independently establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 3D–F adds explicit Pareto-frontier analyses comparing performance and inference cost across default and tuned configurations. The synthetic local-feature demonstration, four AGOP interpretability case studies and Covertype scaling comparison remain; no new robustness-testing or component-ablation program is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions average meta-test results over five train/test splits and report Wilcoxon comparisons against KRR and original RFM with p < 0.0001. v2 adds no confidence intervals, seed counts or new uncertainty-reporting practice for its additional results.

E6.justification: Numerous xRFM outcomes are replaced alongside revised search settings: Table B.1's regression SGM changes from 0.315 to 0.311, and Table B.4's average rank from 8.83 to 5.96. Meta-test scores also change, and TabArena results are added. However, binary Table B.10 duplicates regression Table B.8 and conflicts with Figure 3F, making its binary entries unreliable.

T1.justification: The general kernel family and positive-definiteness condition are equivalent after interchanging p and q notation. AGOP and metric definitions and the asymptotic complexity arguments are retained. No new theorem, proof or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a claim that xRFM lies on the regression performance–inference-time Pareto frontier on TabArena-Lite and remains competitive on classification. The central TALENT performance, scalability and native AGOP interpretability contributions are retained.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces v1's assertion of empirically linear total runtime with an explanation of initially superlinear scaling followed by log-linear scaling once partitioning begins around 60,000 samples. It also adds the TabArena Pareto interpretation. Existing interpretability explanations and future-work limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly identifies the KerMac GPU library and its repository, while Table A.1 adds TabArena hyperparameter ranges and kernel sampling probabilities. However, Appendix A.1's stated kernel choices conflict with the revised table. The original xRFM code-access information remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Elo rating reference and replaces the 2013 OpenML citation with a distinct 2025 retrospective. TabArena receives expanded benchmarking discussion, but the positioning relative to RFM, scalable kernels and tree-based models remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose, tense and terminology edits, integrates TabArena into Section 4, condenses the interpretability dataset list and revises kernel notation. The overall section order and appendix organization remain.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from three to six panels, adding Elo/inference-time axes, configuration markers and Pareto curves. Table A.1 gains a benchmark column and sampling rows, and Tables B.8–B.10 introduce extensive additional displays. Several existing figures move, while the synthetic and AGOP visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: The added TabArena evaluation, probability-sensitive classification metrics and correction of v1's empirical scaling explanation strengthen the paper. However, v2's new binary Table B.10 reproduces regression Table B.8 and contradicts Figure 3F, while Appendix A.1 conflicts with Table A.1 about kernel sampling. These introduced reliability and reproducibility problems leave the net quality benefit uncertain.
